definitions.explanation: The mechanical device in a camera that controls exposure time by opening and closing to allow light onto the film or sensor.
A metal or wooden door that rolls down or folds to close a storefront, garage, or window.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From English "shutter."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- シャッター⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to press the shutter, take a photo)
- シャッター⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}す→押す：02854_osu⟧ (to press the shutter)
- シャッター⟦スピード→スピード：11048_supiido⟧ (shutter speed)
- シャッター⟦チャンス→チャンス：03857_chansu⟧ (photo opportunity)
- シャッター⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|お}ろす→下ろす：02029_orosu⟧ (to close the shutter/rolling door)
- シャッター⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧ (to open the shutter/rolling door)

SOCIAL CONTEXT: シャッター⟦{街|がい}→街：17306_machi⟧ (shuttered shopping street) and シャッター⟦{通|どお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧ (shuttered street) are terms describing the decline of local shopping districts where many stores have permanently closed, a common sight in rural Japan due to population decline and competition from large retailers.
